items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I arranged for him about seven years. He had a very progressive band for a time, yes.

ctx.x: He went to Europe, you know.

That's right, he went to Europe, that's right. He went to Europe and the next year, Paschal, who used to play with Henderson. Paschal came in, Paschal got the band, he hired me as banjoist and ranger. Oh, I had made some arrangements for King's band, and incidentally, this might seem humorous, one of the boys came up to me and said, have you heard Red Nichols and Biff Moe play Ida, Sweeties Appleside? I said, yeah, I got the record. He said, why don't you steal that arrangement, arranging for the band. I said,…
A very progressive band, yes. A young Chicago kid.

items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: so I started taking lessons from Elger.

ctx.x: There weren't any jazz men around Chicago?

No, there weren't any then. They were all playing, they were all playing Scott Joplin Rags then. And, uh, Elger came from, up from New Orleans, and by knowing my mother from New Orleans, she came. And, uh, they said that Charles had started studying violin, but it didn't do no good. Maybe it was the teacher, or maybe it was him. And so, uh, they brought my violin out, and Elger said, my goodness, they said, man, shouldn't have had a full-size violin like that to teach you? He said, so I started taking lessons…
Was it mainly brass music, or did you hear violin music, too?
